title: Enterprise E-Commerce Returns, Reverse Logistics Grading, Switch-Fraud Detection & Re-Commerce Pricing Agent

tiers.tier: Tier 1: Blanket Free-Return Labels + Central Warehouse Manual Grading
tiers.architecture: Shipping every returned item (even $14 apparel) back to a central warehouse for $11.50 freight/touch + manual visual grading + bulk pallet liquidation

tiers.tier: Tier 2: Prompt-Only General LLM Return Chatbot + Unverified Instant Refunds
tiers.architecture: Customer-facing LLM chat issuing instant 'Keep It' refunds when users claim 'arrived damaged' + easily gamed by AI-edited defect photos

tiers.tier: Tier 3: Static Return-Rate Threshold (>35% Ban) + Basic Rules Routing
tiers.architecture: Blocking customers whose return count exceeds 35% (accidentally banning high-LTV multi-size fashion buyers) without SKU recovery MILP or serial/weight verification

tiers.tier: Tier 4: Net-CLV Bracket Router + In-Dropoff Weight/Serial/VLM Fraud Gate + Disposition MILP Agent
tiers.architecture: Net-CLV Margin Scoring (Protects Multi-Size VIPs) + Drop-Off Kiosk Weight/OCR-Serial/ELA-VLM Gate + Multi-Echelon Refurbish/Peer-to-Peer/Outlet MILP

scenarios.scenario: Reverse-Freight Negative-Margin Trap ($16 Fast-Fashion Top with $12.80 Shipping + Restock Cost)
scenarios.question: A trusted 4-year customer (Net CLV = +$1,420) initiates a return on a $16 seasonal t-shirt where reverse shipping + warehouse touch costs $12.80 and liquidation yields $2.10
scenarios.model_answer: Evaluate Disposition Expected Net Recovery: E[R_ship] = $2.10 - $12.80 = -$10.70 < $0; trigger 'Refund & Keep / Local Charity Drop' or peer-to-peer local forward, saving $10.70 net loss
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 1 mails a prepaid UPS label and processes the $16 shirt through 4 warehouse touches, losing $10.70 MORE than simply letting the trusted buyer keep it.

scenarios.scenario: High-Value Electronics 'Brick-in-Box / Counterfeit Swap' Fraud ($1,199 GPU / Headphones)
scenarios.question: First-time burner account initiates return on a $1,199 GPU claiming 'unopened box', but drops off a resealed box containing a 2016 old GPU card
scenarios.model_answer: Withhold instant refund; require package-less drop-off kiosk scan verifying sub-gram load-cell weight profile + PCB serial/QR laser-etch OCR before releasing funds (0.0% swap escape)
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 2 issues an 'instant refund on carrier first scan' the moment the fraudster drops the brick-stuffed box at a parcel locker ($1,199 total loss).

scenarios.scenario: Protecting High-LTV 'Bracket Buyers' vs. Event 'Wardrobing' Abuse
scenarios.question: Customer A buys $4,800/yr in dresses (orders sizes S, M, L and returns S & L unworn within 4 days = 66% return rate, Net Margin +$1,150); Customer B buys a $950 gala gown, wears it on Saturday night, and returns Monday with perfume/hem wear
scenarios.model_answer: Score Net Contribution Margin (Gross Margin Kept - Return Handling Cost) instead of raw return %; whitelist Customer A for instant boxless exchange while flagging Customer B for physical tag/UV inspection
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 3's static '>35% return rate ban' blocks Customer A (losing $1,150/yr profit and causing 14.6% VIP churn) while missing Customer B's single-order gala wardrobing.

scenarios.scenario: Seasonal Apparel & Open-Box Electronics Multi-Channel Disposition MILP
scenarios.question: Route 1,500 daily returned winter parkas in late January across local retail store restock, central steamed refurbishment, Certified Open-Box marketplace, or bulk liquidators
scenarios.model_answer: Solve time-decay price elasticity MILP: route Grade-A directly from drop-off kiosk to nearest store with stockout demand in 2.4 days (recovering 88% retail price vs. 18% liquidator pennies)
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 1 ships all parkas to a central hub where they sit in a 24-day backlog until winter ends, forcing a 15-cents-on-the-dollar liquidation dump.

perturbation_checks.check: Post-Holiday January 'Returnageddon' 3.5x Volume Surge (540,000 Returns in 14 Days)
perturbation_checks.perturbed: 80.2% Net Value Recovery | 2.8d Shelf Cycle (Direct Store-to-Consumer Bypass Active)

perturbation_checks.check: Generative AI Inpainting Attack ('Fake Shattered Screen / Torn Seam' Overlay on Product Photo)
perturbation_checks.perturbed: 0.0% Switch/Fake-Damage Fraud Escape (EXIF/ELA + Physical Kiosk Verification)

key_findings: Tier 4 (Net-CLV Bracket Router + Drop-Off Weight/Serial/VLM Fraud Gate + Multi-Channel Disposition MILP) boosts net returned-merchandise value recovery from 38.0% to 81.5% and compresses return-to-resale shelf cycle time from 24.0 days to 2.4 days.

Evaluating customers on Net Contribution Margin (Gross Margin Kept minus Reverse Logistics Cost) rather than crude return-rate percentages eliminates false bans on profitable multi-size 'bracket' VIPs (0.0% vs. 14.6% VIP churn).

Gating high-value refunds on package-less drop-off kiosk load-cell weight and serial/PCB OCR verification eliminates 100% of brick-in-box and counterfeit-swap fraud (0.0% vs. 18.4%), cutting monthly reverse-logistics and fraud losses from $860K to $92K (-89.3%).
